🚨 बॉलीवुड में छाया गैंगस्टर का खौफ! AICWA ने Devendra Fadnavis से मांगी कड़ी सुरक्षा! 🎬

All Indian Cine Workers Association (AICWA) के प्रेसिडेंट Suresh Shyamlal Gupta ने महाराष्ट्र के गृह मंत्री Devendra Fadnavis और मुंबई पुलिस कमिश्नर Deven Bharti को लेटर लिखकर सुरक्षा की गुहार लगाई है। एसोसिएशन का दावा है कि गैंगस्टरों ने Saif Ali Khan, Amitabh Bachchan और Abhishek Bachchan को धमकी दी है और उनके पास 200 शूटर्स होने का दावा किया है।

अक्टूबर में Juhu में हुई Tiger Shroff वाली फायरिंग की घटना के बाद से पूरी इंडस्ट्री में डर का माहौल है। AICWA के मुताबिक इस खौफ की वजह से शूटिंग की रफ्तार धीमी पड़ गई है, जिससे दिहाड़ी मजदूरों, तकनीशियनों और कलाकारों की रोजी-रोटी पर असर पड़ रहा है।

असोसिएशन ने सरकार के सामने 5 मुख्य मांगें रखी हैं, जिनमें स्टार्स और उनके परिवारों की सुरक्षा, शूटिंग लोकेशंस पर पुलिस प्रोटेक्शन और गैंगस्टरों पर सख्त एक्शन शामिल है। AICWA का कहना है कि बॉलीवुड बिना किसी डर के काम कर सके, यही उनका मकसद है। 🚓

क्या आपको लगता है कि मुंबई पुलिस को बॉलीवुड स्टार्स की सुरक्षा तुरंत बढ़ा देनी चाहिए? अपनी राय कमेंट्स में जरूर बताएं! 👇

ctx.text:
The association has urged the Maharashtra government and Mumbai Police to step up protection for film personalities and shooting locations.
The All Indian Cine Workers Association (AICWA) has approached the Maharashtra government and Mumbai Police, seeking urgent security measures for Bollywood personalities following alleged threats from gangsters. AICWA President Suresh Shyamlal Gupta has written to Maharashtra Chief Minister and Home Minister Devendra Fadnavis, with a copy of the representation marked to Mumbai Police Commissioner Deven Bharti, requesting protection for actors, filmmakers and other members of the film fraternity.
In a statement shared on X (formerly Twitter), the association expressed concern over the reported threats directed at actors Saif Ali Khan, Amitabh Bachchan and Abhishek Bachchan. According to AICWA, gangsters have allegedly issued threats to the actors and claimed to have 200 shooters at their disposal. The association said the situation has raised concerns about the safety of people working in the entertainment industry.
The representation comes amid heightened security concerns in Mumbai following the October firing incident involving actor Tiger Shroff in Juhu, as well as recent threat warnings reportedly directed at Saif Ali Khan and Amitabh Bachchan.
AICWA has also pointed to the impact of these developments on film production activities across the city. According to the association, concerns over security have slowed down shooting schedules, potentially affecting the livelihoods of daily-wage workers, technicians, set workers and artists who depend on regular film assignments.
The association has placed five demands before the state government and Mumbai Police. These include enhanced security for Saif Ali Khan, Amitabh Bachchan, Abhishek Bachchan and their families; safety measures for film personalities and filmmakers across Mumbai; adequate police protection at shooting locations; strict action against gangsters and their networks; and close monitoring of press conferences and public events involving film personalities.
Emphasising the film industry's contribution to employment in Maharashtra, AICWA said that those working in cinema should be able to carry out their professional commitments without intimidation. The association concluded its appeal by stating, “Bollywood must be able to move freely on Mumbai's streets, shoot and work without fear.”
